# Chapter Twelve: Training

Two weeks later Victor stepped off a plane bookended by the two priests at the Glasgow Airport in Scotland. He was quickly ushered into a car and they sped away from the airport. “Where is my family” Victor asked again for the hundredth time. Sam who had been incensed by the way the Bishop had handled Vic’s recruitment had taken care of the family, ensured they wanted for nothing and that they now had new lives, they were told that a drug gang from one of Vic’s investigations had targeted the family and had killed Vic, they were moved into protective custody, made easier by the fact that she was an only child and her parents had passed in an accident 5 years prior.

“Vic, you know I can’t tell you that, but know that I personally took care of it, they will want for nothing and they are living someplace comfortably, that is all I can say” Victor looked out the window and not at his old friend as the city zipped by him, looking grey and old, much like he felt right now. “How was my funeral” he asked bitterly knowing that Sam had presided over it as one of his oldest friends, Jessica had asked him to, Vic found this funny, sad but funny that one of the men responsible for taking him away from them was honored to give his eulogy. “it was a wonderful ceremony, the churched spared no expense and ensured that the family had to pay nothing, they of course were told it was from a life insurance policy you had taken out, as was there new found wealth, they accepted it of course” Sam said looking at his old friend. Vic had been distant these last few weeks seeming to keep to himself and to spend time with the weapons as his only companions, Sam wasn’t sure what he saw but knew it had changed his friend, he had learned how to hunt and how to kill an enemy he would have laughed had you told him existed just three weeks ago.

“Well now that you have me on the ground, you want to tell me what we are doing here” Vic asked both priests. Bishop Talbot who had been reviewing something he had pulled from his briefcase looked up ‘hunting my boy, we are meeting Edgar here and you two are going to hunt down a pack of wolves who have been killing along backroads of the Dundee countryside” Talbot closed the binder and put it away. This is your initial hunt, Edgar will judge whether you are ready to go out on your own, but the first hunt is always with an experienced hunter. Vic nodded, he had thought as much, he had spent so much time living through Alfonso as he trained he literally knew the man better then himself and understood the orders process, he had spent the last two weeks buried in the memories of his ancestor and learned how to track and use the weapons, but they still seemed weak to him, even the words of power were weak compared to when Alfonso used them in the visions, Sam told him it had to do with Faith, that the more faith in god he had, the stronger the weapons became. He didn’t know if it was true, but Vic’s faith in god had been shaken, badly, he didn’t know If he could get it back. Not after his parent’s death, the limo careened towards there safe house in Scotland, And he definitely didn’t trust the church, that was for sure he thought, and gazed at the two men across from him with resentment in his eyes and heart.

Edgar was there waiting for them when they pulled up to the old Scottish Manor outside of Dundee, it was a modest two story Stone home with outbuildings spread across 10 acres. One of the churches many properties he was told. As they crossed to the front door. Talbot turned to Edgar “get him settled and you two should spend some time together before you go out, we will be here if you need us” and with that the Bishop followed Sam into the house and shut the door. Edgar shook his head and chuckled “Still the same old Talbot, the man is a raging ass clown” and he turned to Vic with that half grin still plastered on his face. As with the first time they met, Vic instantly liked the guy and he seemed to have an issue with Talbot, which made Vic like him all the more. “Yeah, I am guessing he was not voted most popular in priest school” Vic said Edgar’s half grin becoming contagious.

“Come on Vic, let’s get you checked in to the presidential suite” he said with a laugh and threw his arm around the smaller man’s shoulder. “It’s good to get another hunter, though I wouldn’t wish the circumstances of your recruitment on anyone, is it true you went head to head with three of them without even knowing they existed” he asked almost in awe Vic nodded, yup, they come for us at the house he said, remembering that night sent a shiver up his spine, “Damn, I just about shit the first time I saw one and I had been trained by that point, what a rude awakening, I am glad your family is okay, some of us have had losses” he said, his smile fading a bit and Vic could see his face darken a little, there was a story there, but bet not to push it now, he thought.

“Yeah the only training I have had is living through someone else, so go easy on me” Vic said. Edgar looked at him in surprise “That’s the way we all get trained, something about the weapon, it knows what you need to learn and it shows it to you, its creepy like that. It also pairs you with someone who you can easily relate to, thus the choice of person you live through. For everyone its different he said as they rounded the corner to the small cottage set back from the house. “He ushered Vic inside and then closed the door, the house smelled like beef stew and damn was that a welcome smell Vic thought as his stomach grumbled “I see I put dinner on just in time” Edgar laughed and then threw open one of the doors off of the main living room and kitchen area. “This is your room, go ahead and get settled, once you do I should have dinner on the table”.

Vic went in and threw his bag on the single bed in the corner, the room was sparse with only the bed and a dresser in the room, covered in flower wallpaper and a hardwood floor that looks like it hadn’t been cared for in about a millennium. Vic sat down and unpacked his bag into the dresser, His weapons would be delivered later coming via diplomatic pouch. He wasn’t sure how they worked that out, they might not have an official name, but they had friends in high places.

Vic came out of the room just in time to see Edgar putting two bowls of steaming stew on the small wooden table in the dining area. “Smells awesome” Vic said taking a seat as Edgar slid into the one across from him. “Dig in, we have a lot to go over and tomorrow night we hunt” he said pointing to Vic’s bowl. They ate in mostly silence disturbed only when a delivery person came to the door with a box for each of them marked “Diplomatic pouch”. Edgar put the boxes next to the door and returned to the table to finish eating. After dinner Vic washed the bowels and Edgar delivered the boxes to each of their rooms and returned with a bottle of Kentucky Bourbon. Vic looked at him, smiled and pulled two glasses out of the cupboard.

Edgar poured two healthy amounts into them and motioned for Vic to come in join him in the living room. The air was getting cold out so Edgar had thrown a fire in the fireplace but left the lights off. And they sat and chatted for a while.

“So how the hell did you end up in this line of work” Vic asked as he sat down, feeling the warmth of the fire even 6 feet from the open flame. He turned to look at the bigger man whose large beard spread into a toothy grin. “I worked a rig in Louisiana when the priests found me, like yours mine wasn’t a known line at the time, I had a DNA test done years before for paternity and apparently the results were flagged in there system, They waited and watched and one day a priest walks up and asks me to join him for lunch, so I do and the rest is history, you see not ever member of the line has whatever it is that allows you to use the weapons so they have to test them to know for sure” Edgar said, taking a healthy gulp out of the glass. Vic thought about that, “So how come I wasn’t tested?” he asked. Which got a laugh out of Edgar who was in the middle of another sip, which ended up somewhere in that void of hair he called a beard. “You were, on the day we found the body, the cross I handed you, that was a relic, I was testing you and you passed, they had your tagged in the system but had never approached you, when the body showed up they thought the wolves might have outed you, but when you showed up to work, they figured it was only a coincidence, they were unfortunately wrong, it seems the pack used the body to out us and you allowing them to track you back to the house and us to our safe house” he said tipping his glass to Vic. ”When they hit your house, they had sent a hunting party to the safe house to hit hunters, we lost 3 good men and women that day” he said his face going dark again. He thought about it and remembered the look on the bigger man’s face when he had said the cross was warm. That must have been the test. “You brought in extra hunters to watch my house didn’t you, but before you could they hit you guys giving them a window at me” he said bitterly, seeing the pattern form. Edgar just nodded and threw back his glass. They formed an unspoken agreement to leave all wolf talk alone for the night.

They talked about life and any other subject other than wolves. As the bottle got lighter, their laughs grew louder until neither one could keep their eyes open.
